source.title: Fixed Point Explainability
source.authors: Emanuele La Malfa; Jon Vadillo; Marco Molinari; Michael J. Wooldridge

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAEs recursively to LLM activations and measures feature overlap and preservation of model answers. Its results bear on whether SAE features are stable and functionally complete, and it reports cases where reconstruction does not preserve the model's answers.
record.gate_note: The paper describes SAEs as producing sparse, interpretable features, but does not test superposition geometry, feature sparsity or importance, polysemanticity, feature recovery against a ground truth, or feature dimensionality. The SAE results recorded here concern recursive feature overlap and answer correctness; KL divergence is not included because it does not directly measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Only the single-pass splice bears on V5. It patches one SAE reconstruction into the residual stream of Llama-3.3-70B and Llama-3.1-8B and checks answer correctness, a standard fidelity/completeness check. Recursive re-encoding (double/constant) is a different construct: whether an SAE is idempotent on its own outputs.
record.authors_conclusion: Roughly right. Authors say pretrained SAEs lack consistency because reconstructions fail to preserve predicted tokens, which undermines trust in their 'disentangled' features. They also claim convergence 100% of the time and faster, more informative fixed points in larger models, hinting at a scaling law. Their text's '93% P-FPE in numerical questions' conflicts with Table 2, where 0.93 is multiple-choice and numerical is 0.0000.
record.recipe_differences: The study recursively applies pretrained SAEs and evaluates explanation consistency and prediction preservation; it does not use the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Question type and recursive SAE iteration setting change the reported answer-correctness outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Recursively re-encoding SAE reconstructions reaches a constant point. Correctness there falls to 0 for 8B on all types and for 70B numerical; 70B MC keeps 0.93 top-1 and 0.99 top-5. Feature overlap with the first pass decays to about 0.002–0.03 Jaccard.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs applied to their own reconstructions are not idempotent and drift to fixed points that destroy the model's predictions.

record.problems: The SAE evaluation uses synthetic single-token-answer questions generated by GPT4. The paper reports no uncertainty for the correctness or Jaccard values, and the supplied flattened table text does not clearly map all Jaccard entries to recursive settings. The paper also does not directly test SAE feature completeness or canonicality against an independent reference.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, the KL divergence results were left out because they do not directly measure the claim versions. No additional Jaccard rows were added beyond the table's reported entries; their setting alignment is unclear.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry, or sparsity transition.
No capacity or importance allocation, no neuron polysemanticity.
No test of whether features are spread across neurons or recovered against ground truth.

Canonicality/uniqueness and stability across seeds, dictionary sizes or layers are untested. Only one layer per model and a small synthetic single-token dataset; interpretability of features is not assessed.

missing.what: KL divergence between original and single-splice logits. 70B: 0.67 numerical, 0.15 MC, 0.93 GK. 8B: 0.15, 0.11, 0.08. A direct reconstruction-fidelity measure that matches the correctness pattern.
missing.locator: Table 2 and Table 5, KL Div column

record.verdict_notes: The SAE evidence is narrow: one layer per model and different SAE sources per model (Goodfire for 70B, EleutherAI for 8B), so model size is confounded with SAE. The dataset is small and GPT-4-generated, with no uncertainty reported. Only single-splice results map to V5 completeness; the recursion results are an out-of-distribution construct, logged under fits_no_version. The reader's 'reversed' states for correctness drops misread the version direction.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy-network superposition, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
The study does not test capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, or allocation of features to dimensions.
The study does not investigate causes of polysemanticity or whether it can occur without capacity pressure.
The study uses SAEs on LLM activations but does not test whether features are spread across neurons or whether an SAE recovers features against a ground truth.

The study examines recursive feature overlap and whether SAE reconstructions preserve answers; it does not establish feature completeness, uniqueness, or canonical status against an independent ground truth.
The study does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-8B (EleutherAI SAE), all question types, and Llama-3.3-70B multiple-choice; single SAE splice
relationships.reason: A single reconstruction preserves top-1/top-5 correctness at or above base (r10, r14, r29, r33, r37, r41, r45, r49).
relationships.display_finding: One reconstruction pass kept top-1 and top-5 correctness at or above the base model.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Llama-3.1-8B (EleutherAI SAE), all question types, and Llama-3.3-70B multiple-choice; single SAE splice
source_check.reason: r10, r14, r29, r37, r41, r45 and r49 preserve or improve correctness; r33 shows nearly full preservation. The supplied reason's at-or-above claim is incorrect for r33: numerical top-5 falls from 0.9802 to 0.9505. Support concerns tested behavioral sufficiency only.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.3-70B (Goodfire SAE), numerical and general-knowledge questions; single SAE splice
relationships.reason: One reconstruction cuts correctness: 0.64 to 0.42 and 0.26 to 0.07 (top-1); top-5 also drops (r2, r6, r18, r22). Reconstruction is incomplete here.
relationships.display_finding: A single SAE reconstruction cut top-1 correctness from 0.64 to 0.42 and from 0.26 to 0.07, and top-5 accuracy also fell, so the reconstruction was incomplete.

source_check.condition: Llama-3.3-70B (Goodfire SAE), numerical and general-knowledge questions; single SAE splice
source_check.reason: r2, r6, r18 and r22 show substantial but incomplete correctness preservation, while multiple-choice correctness is preserved.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study directly measures answer correctness after substituting SAE reconstructions into LLM hidden representations.

tranche.reason: Single-reconstruction results show task-dependent failures of behavioral sufficiency, qualifying V5 completeness.

source_check.notes: Tables report answer correctness, which does not establish canonical units or exact prediction preservation. Section 4.3 assigns 93% P-FPE to numerical questions, but Table 2 places 0.9300 under multiple-choice constant reconstruction; numerical constant correctness is 0.0000.

statements.correction: Llama-3.3-70B single reconstruction: numerical top-1 0.6436 → 0.4158; general-knowledge top-1 0.2647 → 0.0686; multiple-choice top-1 0.9700 → 0.9700. Verdict for numerical/general-knowledge conditions: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The numerical losses are correct, but the challenges label overstates this study's partial preservation under the verdict rules.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Llama-3.3-70B and Llama-3.1-8B, multiple-choice tasks, single and double SAE iterations
reader_labels.reason: Several reported correctness values match the base condition, but this is limited to the tested question type and iteration counts; see r10-r11, r14-r15, r41-r42, r46, and r50.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Numerical and General-Knowledge tasks at the constant point on both Llama models
reader_labels.reason: The constant-point reconstructions have 0.0000 reported top-token and top-five correctness in these task groups; see r4, r8, r20, r24, r31, r35, r47, and r51.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Numerical and General-Knowledge tasks after one or two SAE iterations, and multiple-choice tasks at the constant point
reader_labels.reason: Answer correctness falls below base in these tested settings, but the size and presence of the decline depend on task type and iteration count; see r2-r3, r6-r7, r12, r18-r19, r22-r23, r29, r33-r34, r39, r45, and r49.
